title: K3 surfaces, Picard lattices and symplectic boundedness
summary: Native K3 geometry over every field, geometric and arithmetic Picard lattices, uniform bounds for finite automorphism subgroups, and fixed-degree polarized moduli over the integers.

layers.title: Native surfaces and the K3 predicate

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsK3
targets.title: One unpolarized predicate
targets.statement: For a field k and f:X→Spec k, define IsK3 f to be SmoothOfRelativeDimension 2 f ∧ IsProper f ∧ GeometricallyIntegral f ∧ Nonempty(det Ω¹_{X/k} ≅ O_X) ∧ H¹(X,O_X)=0. It is a proposition, with no chosen trivialization, polarization or embedding.
hypotheses: X a native Scheme with f:X→Spec k

locator.where: Chapter 1 Definition 1.1, p.7; huybrechts lines 133–146

targets.proofSketch: Use the native module sheaf and its determinant; H¹ is the module cohomology supplied with duality. Smooth dimension2 makes det Ω¹=∧²Ω¹.

api.name: IsK3.mk
api.statement: The five conditions construct a proof of IsK3.

api.name: IsK3.iff_conditions
api.statement: IsK3 is equivalent to precisely the five displayed conditions.

api.name: IsK3.canonicalIso
api.statement: The smooth dualizing line identifies canonically with det Ω¹; any isomorphism with O is existential.

targets.name: isK3_iso_and_fieldExtension_iff
targets.title: Isomorphisms and arbitrary field extension
targets.statement: For every isomorphism over k the K3 predicate is invariant; for every extension K/k, IsK3(X_K/K) ↔ IsK3(X/k). These equivalences respect identity extensions and towers.

locator.where: Chapter 17 §2.1, p.365; huybrechts lines 13964–13970

targets.proofSketch: Descent and base change handle relative smoothness, properness, dimension and geometric integrality. Flat coherent base change handles H¹ and differentials. For a line bundle on a proper geometrically integral scheme, triviality is equivalent to nonzero global sections of it and its inverse; their nonzero product is a constant, so they trivialize it. Faithfulness detects the two nonzero spaces over k.

tests.name: identity_extension
tests.statement: K=k gives identity transport.

tests.name: inseparable_extension
tests.statement: The equivalence includes purely inseparable extensions.

tests.name: rescale_form
tests.statement: Multiplying a geometric volume form by a nonzero scalar changes no predicate.

targets.name: IsK3.projective
targets.title: Projectivity over the original field
targets.statement: Every K3 surface over an arbitrary field k is projective over k.
hypotheses: k an arbitrary field, including imperfect fields

locator.where: Chapter 1 Remark 1.2, p.7; huybrechts line 147

targets.proofSketch: Apply the general smooth proper surface projectivity theorem required from the scheme owner, with relative smoothness of dimension2 and geometric integrality supplied by1.1. The supplier contract retains its full arbitrary-field surface statement and its modification/ample-support proof. Projectivity is not inferred merely from projectivity after algebraic closure.

tests.name: plane_projective
tests.statement: A smooth quartic has O(1) as an ample witness; it satisfies the native predicate rather than carrying an embedding as data.

tests.name: dimension_control

tests.name: imperfect_control
tests.statement: Relative smoothness is retained over imperfect k; regularity alone is not the stated hypothesis.

targets.name: IsK3.riemannRoch
targets.title: Coherent invariants and contraction
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X/k, ω=∧²Ω¹, h⁰(O)=h²(O)=1, χ(O)=2 and 2χ(L)=4+L² in ℤ for every invertible L. For each nonzero σ∈H⁰(ω), v↦(w↦σ(v,w)) identifies T_X with Ω¹_X; scaling σ scales this map.
hypotheses: L invertible; σ nonzero for contraction

locator.where: Chapter 1 §2.3 equation (2.5), pp.11–12; huybrechts lines 142,305,316

targets.proofSketch: Proper geometric integrality identifies global functions with k; Serre duality gives h². Apply surface RR geometrically and transport Euler characteristics and intersections by base change. A local frame computes contraction.

tests.name: rr_unit
tests.statement: L=O gives 2χ=4, including characteristic2: division never occurs in k.

tests.name: rr_quartic
tests.statement: For a quartic hyperplane H, H²=4 and χ(H)=4.

tests.name: contraction_frame
tests.statement: If σ(e₁,e₂)=1, e₁ maps to e₂* and e₂ to -e₁*; in characteristic2 the latter sign becomes plus.

targets.name: IsK3.numericalKernel_eq_zero
targets.title: Numerical and torsion kernels
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X/k, a line-bundle class whose intersection with every class of Pic(X) is zero is trivial. In particular Pic(X) has no nontrivial torsion, in any characteristic.

locator.where: Chapter 1 Proposition 2.4 and Remark 2.5, p.12; huybrechts lines 335–354

targets.proofSketch: Fix a k-ample H. A nontrivial L with L·H=0 has no section, nor does its inverse, since every nonzero effective divisor has positive H-intersection. Duality gives χ(L)≤0; numerical triviality and RR give χ(L)=2. Torsion is numerically trivial by cancellation in integer intersections.

tests.name: torsion_p
tests.statement: The argument also excludes p-torsion in characteristic p.

tests.name: effective_minus_two
tests.statement: A smooth rational curve C has C²=-2 by adjunction and is not numerically trivial.

tests.name: unit_kernel
tests.statement: O belongs to the kernel and is its only element.

targets.name: smoothQuartic_isK3
targets.title: Quartics over every field
targets.statement: For every field k, a smooth quartic hypersurface X⊂P³_k is K3, with H=O_X(1), H²=4 and χ(O_X(t))=2t²+2 for all integers t. The Fermat quartic is smooth exactly when char k≠2.
hypotheses: smoothness of the quartic for its K3 assertion

locator.where: Chapter 1 Example 1.3(i), p.8; huybrechts lines 160–183

targets.proofSketch: The hypersurface and conormal sequences compute H¹ and ω. Smooth geometric connectedness gives integrality. Bézout gives H², then RR gives the polynomial. Fermat partials are 4x_i³.

tests.name: quartic_t0
tests.statement: χ(O)=2 although h⁰(O)=1.

tests.name: fermat_F2
tests.statement: Over F₂ the equation is (Σx_i)⁴=0, a nonreduced thickening.

layers.examples: Smooth quartics, the empty scheme, P², and products of elliptic curves distinguish the predicate; the quartic polynomial gives χ(O)=2 and χ(O(1))=4.

layers.title: Picard spaces, vanishing and lifting

targets.name: IsK3.relativePicardSpace
targets.title: The relative Picard space
targets.statement: For a smooth proper finitely presented algebraic-space family X→S whose geometric fibres are K3 schemes, represent the fppf sheaf T↦Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) by a separated algebraic space locally of finite presentation. It is unramified, has trivial fibrewise identity and torsion subfunctors, and commutes with arbitrary base change. Over a field it is an étale group scheme.
hypotheses: each geometric fibre a native K3 scheme

locator.where: Theorem 3.1.1, Lemma 3.1.2, Proposition 3.1.3, pp.9–11; rizov lines 404,416,440

targets.proofSketch: Apply general representability and its tangent formula. H¹(O)=0 makes the tangent zero; over fields the identity is a reduced point, and 1.5 eliminates torsion. Relative unramifiedness follows from geometric fibres and finite presentation, not from relative flatness.

api.name: relativePicardSpace.baseChange

api.name: relativePicardSpace.ext

api.name: relativePicardSpace.tangent

api.name: relativePicardSpace.arithmeticPoints

targets.name: IsK3.regularOneForms_closed
targets.title: The positive-characteristic closedness theorem
targets.statement: For every K3 surface in characteristic p>0, the differential d:H⁰(X,Ω¹)→H⁰(X,Ω²) is zero.

locator.where: Theorem 1.3, pp.172–173; lang-nygaard lines 76–104

targets.proofSketch: Extend to an algebraic closure, a perfect field. Finite-height formal Brauer gives Hodge–de Rham degeneration by Nygaard Corollary2.7. In infinite height, Serre duality turns a nonzero differential into injectivity on H²(O); FdV=d then forces any Witt differential kernel into every image of V, contradicting the separate kernel theorem. The kernel theorem and its unirationality input remain explicit gaps.

tests.name: closed_char_two
tests.statement: No division by2 or restriction p>2 occurs.

tests.name: zero_form
tests.statement: The zero one-form is closed.

tests.name: no_automatic_surface_degeneration

targets.name: IsK3.noVectorFields
targets.title: Vanishing in all characteristics
targets.statement: For every K3 surface over every field, H⁰(X,Ω¹)=H⁰(X,T_X)=H²(X,T_X)=0.

locator.where: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, pp.171–172; lang-nygaard lines 54–74; characteristic-zero branch huybrechts line 379

targets.proofSketch: In positive characteristic, all forms and their Cartier iterates are closed. Oda identifies them as an image of p-torsion Picard Dieudonné data; this is zero by 2.1. Contraction and duality give the tangent vanishings. In characteristic zero spread out to a finitely generated field, embed it into C, use proper GAGA and projective Kähler Hodge symmetry h¹⁰=h⁰¹=0, then descend.

tests.name: abelian_surface_control
tests.statement: An abelian surface has nonzero invariant vector fields and is excluded by H¹(O).

tests.name: identity_tangent
tests.statement: The automorphism functor has zero tangent at the identity.

tests.name: char2_vanishing
tests.statement: The theorem includes p=2.

targets.name: IsK3.hodgeAndCrystallineRanks
targets.title: Hodge numbers and integral crystalline modules
targets.statement: For a K3 surface over any field, h^{p,q}=dim H^q(Ω^p) is 1 at (0,0),(2,0),(0,2),(2,2), 20 at (1,1), and 0 otherwise. In characteristic p>0 over perfect k, Hⁱ_crys(X/W(k)) is free of ranks (1,0,22,0,1), zero outside 0≤i≤4, and the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at E₁.
hypotheses: k perfect for crystalline cohomology over W(k)

locator.where: Proposition 1.1, pp.59–60; deligne-lift lines 29–57; huybrechts line 367

targets.proofSketch: Noether gives c₂=24. RR for Ω¹ gives χ(Ω¹)=-20; 2.3 and duality leave h¹¹=20. The positions in the diamond force all spectral differentials to vanish. Use the generic degree-one crystalline/Picard comparison and crystalline duality to get rational ranks0 in degrees1,3; crystalline Gauss–Bonnet gives rank22 in degree2. Apply the universal-coefficient sequence degree by degree to eliminate integral torsion; do not equate rational ranks with freeness.

tests.name: euler24
tests.statement: The de Rham Euler sum is 1+22+1=24.

tests.name: h11_twenty
tests.statement: χ(Ω¹)=-20, with H⁰=H²=0.

tests.name: hodge_outside
tests.statement: Exterior degree>2 and coherent degree>2 give zero.

targets.name: IsK3.formalDeformation
targets.title: Unpolarized formal deformations
targets.statement: For geometric K3 X/k in characteristic p>0, its marked deformation functor on Artinian local W(k)-algebras with residue k is prorepresented by Spf W(k)[[t₁,…,t₂₀]], up to noncanonical coordinates. In characteristic zero use Artinian local k-algebras and Spf k[[t₁,…,t₂₀]].

locator.where: Corollary 1.2, p.60; deligne-lift line 58; rizov Proposition 4.1.1 line 756

targets.proofSketch: The supplied cotangent/deformation theory has automorphisms H⁰(T)=0, tangent H¹(T) of dimension20 and obstruction H²(T)=0. Apply its prorepresentability and lifting criterion with the fixed marking.

tests.name: dual_numbers20
tests.statement: First-order marked deformations form a 20-dimensional tangent space.

tests.name: marking_required
tests.statement: The unmarked global moduli groupoid can have finite automorphisms; the formal marked functor is the one prorepresented.

targets.name: IsK3.lineBundleDeformationDivisor
targets.title: Line-bundle deformation loci
targets.statement: For geometric K3 X/k in characteristic p>0 and a nontrivial line-bundle class L, the marked pair deformation functor is a closed formal subfunctor of 2.5 defined by one equation and flat over W(k), of relative dimension19. If L is ample of square2d and p∤2d, it is formally smooth. In characteristic zero an ample L gives a formally smooth dimension19 locus.
hypotheses: L nontrivial; ampleness for smoothness clauses

locator.where: Proposition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp.60–62; deligne-lift lines 78,131; rizov Lemma4.1.3 line779

targets.proofSketch: H¹(O)=0 gives uniqueness of class extension and H²(O)=k gives one equation. Deligne’s Gauss–Manin/Kodaira–Spencer argument shows this equation is not divisible by p for nontrivial L: crystalline c₁ cannot remain in F² throughout the universal characteristic-p deformation. At p∤2d, c₁²=2d≠0 makes its tangent obstruction functional nonzero, giving smoothness.

tests.name: trivial_line_control
tests.statement: L=O extends everywhere and has dimension20; nontriviality is essential.

tests.name: bad_degree_control
tests.statement: At p|2d only flatness of the pair locus is asserted.

tests.name: good_degree_dim19
tests.statement: One nonzero linear obstruction cuts the tangent dimension from20 to19.

targets.name: IsK3.polarizedLift
targets.title: A polarized characteristic-zero lift
targets.statement: For a K3 surface over algebraically closed k of characteristic p>0 and any ample L, there is a complete DVR R finite over W(k), a smooth proper R-scheme 𝓧, a relatively ample 𝓛, and a marked special-fibre isomorphism (𝓧_k,𝓛_k)≅(X,L).
hypotheses: k algebraically closed of characteristic p>0

locator.where: Corollaries 1.7–1.8, pp.62–63; deligne-lift lines 140–160

targets.proofSketch: Use the flat pair-deformation divisor to find a finite trait in it: a parameter quotient followed by normalization gives R. Algebraize the ample formal line and formal surface by Grothendieck existence; smoothness and ampleness extend from the closed fibre. This is existence of a suitable lift, not liftability along every fixed deformation.

tests.name: p2_lift
tests.statement: R may be ramified, including p=2.

tests.name: not_every_lift
tests.statement: The conclusion supplies a chosen trait; it does not make the pair deformation space smooth at every bad prime.

layers.examples: The positive-power vanishing excludes O; characteristic2 remains in the closed-form and lifting arguments. A trivial line deforms everywhere, so it cannot define a flat dimension19 divisor.

targets.statement: On the supplied Hausdorff second-countable native complex-manifold carrier, IsK3Analytic M means M is compact, nonempty and connected, of complex dimension2, with analytically trivial canonical line and H¹(M,O)=0.

locator.where: Chapter1 Definition3.1, p.14; huybrechts lines 405–407

targets.proofSketch: Use the supplied analytic sheaf and canonical bundle; this is a predicate on that carrier, with no parallel analytic-space category.

targets.name: IsK3.analytification
targets.title: GAGA and the projective essential image
targets.statement: For algebraic K3 X/C, X_an is an analytic K3, with natural coherent-cohomology, canonical-line and Picard comparisons preserving tensor products, pullbacks and contraction. An analytic K3 is algebraizable as an algebraic K3 exactly when it has a holomorphic closed embedding in some Pⁿ(C).

locator.where: Chapter1 Proposition3.2 and ensuing paragraph, p.14; huybrechts lines 408–429

tests.name: gaga_volume

tests.name: projective_image

targets.name: IsK3.complexIntegralBetti
targets.title: Integral topology of projective complex K3 surfaces
targets.statement: For a projective analytic K3 M, Hⁱ(M,ℤ) is free of ranks (1,0,22,0,1), zero outside degrees0–4. Its Hodge decomposition has h²⁰=h⁰²=1 and h¹¹=20; c₁:Pic(M)→H²(M,ℤ) is injective, with image ker(H²(ℤ)→H²(O)), and intersection is cup product evaluated on the complex orientation.

locator.where: Chapter1 §§3.2–3.3, pp.15–17; huybrechts lines 452–511

targets.proofSketch: Hodge symmetry yields H¹(C)=0 and the exponential sequence gives integral H¹=0 and Pic injection. If nx lies in Pic, the map to H²(O), a complex vector space, detects nx=0; Pic has no torsion, eliminating torsion in H². Integral Poincaré duality and universal coefficients then eliminate torsion in H³ and force H³=0. Noether/Gauss–Bonnet gives b₂=22 and Hodge decomposition gives20.

tests.name: complex_orientation
tests.statement: For a quartic hyperplane c₁(H), its cup square integrates to4.

tests.name: torsion_control

targets.name: IsK3.integralEtaleRanks
targets.title: Integral geometric étale invariants
targets.statement: For every K3 X/k and prime ℓ invertible in k, Hⁱ_et(X_kbar,ℤ_ℓ) is free with ranks (1,0,22,0,1), vanishes outside 0≤i≤4, and its degree2 cup-trace pairing with the appropriate Tate twists is perfect.
hypotheses: ℓ prime and invertible in k

locator.where: §2.4, pp.7–8; rizov lines 273–300

targets.proofSketch: Over C use target3.3, then integral singular/étale comparison. In positive characteristic lift by2.7 and compare compatible ℤ/ℓⁿ systems by smooth proper base change before taking the adic limit. Duality supplies the pairing.

tests.name: ell2_allowed

tests.name: h0_trace
tests.statement: H⁰=ℤ_ℓ and the trace of the class of a geometric point in H⁴(2) is1.

layers.examples: The projective quartic agrees on both carriers. A complex two-torus fails H¹(O)=0. Integral cohomology is free, not merely of rational rank22.

layers.title: Picard lattices and arithmetic rank boundedness

targets.name: IsK3.picardBaseChange
targets.title: Picard pullback and arithmetic descent
targets.statement: For K3 X/k and every extension K/k, Pic(X)→Pic(X_K) is injective and preserves intersections, and is bijective when k is algebraically closed. Every geometric line-bundle class descends to a finite extension. A purely inseparable extension of degree pⁿ has Picard cokernel killed by pⁿ. For separable Galois extensions the Picard–Brauer sequence identifies Pic(X)⊗ℚ with the Galois-invariant geometric Picard group tensor ℚ.
hypotheses: separable Galois extension for the last assertion
targets.proofSketch: Injectivity uses nonzero sections of L and L⁻¹. Field base change preserves the Euler-characteristic intersection formula. Over an algebraically closed base the discrete étale Picard scheme makes a spread-out class constant. Descent over finite extensions follows from finite presentation. The pⁿ-power cocycle descends through purely inseparable extensions. Hochschild–Serre and Hilbert90 give the Brauer obstruction, killed after tensoring ℚ.

tests.name: picard_identity
tests.statement: The identity field extension gives the identity map.

tests.name: closed_extension
tests.statement: C⊂K adds no Picard classes.

tests.name: obstruction_control
tests.statement: An invariant geometric class need not be represented over k; no integral Galois-invariant identification is unconditional.

targets.name: IsK3.picardLattice
targets.title: The geometric lattice realization
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X/k, Pic(X) is free of finite rank ρ and its intersection form realizes a nondegenerate even integral lattice of signature (1,ρ−1) on the image of Pic(X) in Pic(X)⊗ℚ. The quotient to the supplied arithmetic numerical divisor group is an isometry. Over algebraically closed k, Pic=NS as well.

locator.where: Chapter1 Proposition2.4, p.12; Chapter17 §2, p.364; huybrechts lines335,13945

targets.proofSketch: Over algebraically closed k use1.5 to identify Pic with Num, whose finiteness and Hodge index are supplied. Over k, inject Pic into geometric Pic to obtain finite freeness; its rational span contains a k-ample positive class, so its orthogonal complement is negative definite. Apply the pinned rational-ambient lattice constructor; the geometry supplies the pairing, not a new abstract carrier.

hypotheses: ℓ invertible for the cycle statement

tests.name: cycle_quartic

targets.name: GeneralLinearGroup.oddCongruenceKernel_torsionFree
targets.title: A general congruence theorem
targets.statement: For every odd prime ℓ and n≥0, ker(GL_n(ℤ_ℓ)→GL_n(𝔽_ℓ)) is torsion-free. Thus reduction is injective on every finite subgroup. Every finite subgroup of GL_n(ℤ) embeds by reduction into GL_n(𝔽₃).

locator.where: Chapter17 proof of Lemma2.6, p.367; huybrechts lines14045–14049 (integral consequence); the p-adic version is derived

targets.proofSketch: For nonidentity I+ℓᵃB with a≥1 minimal and B nonzero modulo ℓ, a coprime positive power has exact leading depth a, and an ℓ-th power has exact depth a+1 by the binomial formula; higher terms have larger valuation for odd ℓ. Iteration excludes finite order. The pinned ext_of_toZModPow separates entries, and mem_span_pow_iff_le_valuation gives a finite leading depth for a nonzero entry, retaining its nonzero hypothesis. Apply to the difference of two elements of a finite subgroup. Embed integral matrices into ℤ₃.

locator.where: Chapter17 Lemma2.6, p.367; huybrechts lines14038–14054

targets.name: IsK3.IsSymplectic

To make pullback a left representation use ρ(f)=(f⁻¹)*; its kernel is the same. The predicate is independent of a nonzero volume-form generator and equivalent before and after any field extension.

targets.statement: For K3 X/k and ample L, the functor of k-scheme automorphisms preserving the relative Picard class of L is represented by a finite étale k-group scheme. targets.title: Uniform embeddings in all characteristics
targets.statement: For K3 X/k and ample L with L²=2d, d>0, L^m is globally generated for m≥2 and very ample for m≥3. The complete system of L³, after choosing a basis, embeds X into P^(9d+1) with Hilbert polynomial9dt²+2. For a K3 scheme family over a Noetherian base with a relatively ample representative L, f_*L³ is locally free of rank9d+2, commutes with arbitrary base change and gives the corresponding relative closed immersion.
hypotheses: Noetherian base and relative representative for the family clause

locator.where: Theorem1.2.2 and Lemma1.2.5, pp.4–5; rizov lines142,169; terakawa Theorem2.4 line354

targets.proofSketch: Apply the general length-(r+1) separation criterion with r=0 for2L and r=1 for3L. For2L, A²≥8; a failure has 0<A·D<2, impossible because A=2L. For3L, A²≥18; failure gives 0<3L·D<4, hence L·D=1, D²≥1 and D²<3/2; evenness of the K3 lattice contradicts D²=1. Higher powers follow similarly. Relative vanishing and the finite-projective cohomology complex give local freeness and arbitrary base change, including nonreduced bases; fibrewise very ampleness gives the closed immersion.

targets.name: k3HilbertLocus
targets.title: The K3 locus inside the projective Hilbert family
targets.statement: In the universal flat projective Hilbert family of surfaces with polynomial9dt²+2, d>0, construct a finite-type locally closed subscheme U_K3 carrying exactly the smooth geometrically integral fibres with H¹(O)=0 and trivial canonical class. The construction and its family commute with base change; every embedded K3 with this polynomial factors through it. Use the scheme-theoretic equality locus of the canonical and zero Picard sections, not merely equality of their ranks.
hypotheses: the Hilbert universal family with the specified polynomial

locator.where: Proposition4.2.1 proof, p.19; rizov lines831–849

targets.proofSketch: First restrict to the open smooth geometrically integral surface locus, then the open H¹(O)=0 locus by semicontinuity. The general relative Picard representative carries the canonical class and zero section; take their scheme-theoretic equality locus. Its separatedness makes this a closed subscheme of that open locus. Relative smoothness identifies the canonical determinant, and the relative Picard trivial class is represented locally by a line pulled back from the base. This is the required K3 family and is finite type. Over arbitrary bases use the finite-presentation descent and cohomology/base-change comparison to establish the universal family statement.

targets.name: polarizedK3HilbertAtlas
targets.title: An actual finite-type covering family
targets.statement: For every d>0 construct a finite-type scheme H_d over ℤ parametrizing linearly normal K3 embeddings into P^(9d+1) of polynomial9dt²+2 whose hyperplane Picard class is3λ for an ample section λ of square2d. It has an open primitive locus H_d^prim and a PGL_(9d+2)-action. Every geometric polarized object is a fibre; every polarized family lies étale-locally in its image after choosing its complete projective frame.

locator.where: Proposition4.2.1 and Theorem4.3.3 Steps1–3, pp.19–24; rizov lines807,1004–1052

targets.proofSketch: Start with the actual K3 locus7.6 and impose linear normality. Use the pullback of[3] along[O(1)] to impose the unique Picard cube-root section, then ampleness and square2d. The root locus is closed within the appropriate K3 Hilbert locus even at3; primitivity is open. Local representatives and frames of f_*L³ give the covering family and its smooth frame-torsor property.

targets.name: polarizedK3ModuliStack
targets.title: The polarized stacks
targets.statement: For every d>0 the étale stacks M_2d and F_2d of7.3 and its primitive subcategory are Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type over Spec ℤ, with F_2d→M_2d an open immersion. There are quotient presentations [H_d/PGL_(9d+2)]≃M_2d and [H_d^prim/PGL_(9d+2)]≃F_2d.

locator.where: Definitions4.3.1–4.3.2 and Theorem4.3.3, pp.20–25; rizov lines879,898,917,964,1004

targets.proofSketch: Effective descent for spaces and Picard sections produces the stack. The frame torsor gives a smooth finite-type atlas and quotient. The graph Hilbert Isom functor is finite type and its tangent is zero, so the diagonal is unramified and the stack is DM. Primitive openness descends from H_d.

targets.name: polarizedK3ModuliStack.separated
targets.title: Trait extension, separation and finite inertia
targets.statement: For d>0, any generic-fibre polarized isomorphism between two smooth proper polarized K3 families over a DVR extends uniquely over that DVR. The diagonals of M_2d and F_2d are finite unramified, so the stacks are separated and have finite inertia.
hypotheses: a DVR for the extension clause

locator.where: Theorem4.3.3 Step5, p.25; rizov lines1075–1085

targets.proofSketch: Étale locally use actual ample representatives on schemes. A K3 has a nonzero regular two-form; a ruled smooth surface has none, so the special fibre is not geometrically ruled. Apply the general trait-extension theorem and descend uniqueness. The proper quasi-finite Isom diagonal is finite; its tangent is zero.

tests.name: not_proper_moduli

targets.statement: For every d>0, M_2d and F_2d have separated coarse moduli algebraic spaces of finite type over Spec ℤ. The coarse map is universal for maps to algebraic spaces and bijects geometric isomorphism classes with geometric points over algebraically closed fields.

tests.name: coarse_twists
